extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies (HR offices), agency counsel, Chief Human Capital Officers (CHCOs), Merit Systems Protection Board practitioners, and Office of Personnel Management staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and standards governing when and how agencies may move positions or employees from the competitive service to the excepted service (or between excepted schedules), the documentation and approvals required, employee notice and appeal rights, and related coverage rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating
rubrics_metrics.description: “Confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating means of a character exclusively associated with a noncareer political appointment that is identified by its close working relationship with the President, head of an agency, or other key appointed officials ... and that carries no expectation of continued employment beyond the presidential administration during which the appointment occurred.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is adopted for use across affected regulations; it identifies positions associated with noncareer political appointments (e.g., Schedule C). The rule also recognizes an alternative interchangeable phrasing: “confidential or policy-determining.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of applicability for movement rules (§302.601)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart applies to any situation where an agency moves a position from the competitive service to the excepted service, or between excepted services, whether pursuant to statute, Executive Order, or an OPM issuance, and to any involuntary movement of an employee who has accrued status and civil service protections under 5 U.S.C. chapter 75, subchapter II, to any position not covered by that chapter or subchapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also applies where a position previously governed by title 5 will be governed by another title going forward, unless the governing statute provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: If directive explicitly lists positions, agency must list positions to OPM
rubrics_metrics.description: When a directing instrument (President, Congress, OPM, or designee) explicitly delineates specific positions to be moved, the agency need only list the positions moved and their organizational locations and provide that list to OPM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the narrowest documentation requirement—no additional criteria explanation required beyond the list and locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: If directive requires selection pursuant to articulated criteria, agency must justify selections
rubrics_metrics.description: If the directive requires the agency to select positions to be moved pursuant to criteria articulated in the directive, the agency must provide OPM a list of positions moved, their locations, and—upon OPM request—an explanation of why the positions met the directive's criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must be prepared to explain how each listed position satisfies the directive's stated criteria when asked by OPM.

rubrics_metrics.name: If directive confers discretion to set objective criteria, agency must supply criteria and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the directive confers discretion on the agency to establish objective criteria for identifying positions or particular slots to be moved, the agency must supply OPM with the list of identified positions or slots, their locations, the objective criteria to be used, and an explanation of how these criteria are relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective criteria must be provided in advance and tied to the rationale for moving the positions; OPM can review relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency documentation and pre-approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must: (1) identify the types, numbers, and locations of positions proposed to be moved; (2) document the basis for the determination that movement is consistent with standards set by the President, Congress, OPM, or designees; (3) obtain CHCO certification that documentation is sufficient and movement is consistent with directive and merit system principles; and (4) submit CHCO certification and supporting documentation to OPM in advance of using the excepted service authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For exceptions effectuated by the President or OPM, agencies must also obtain written approval from the OPM Director before listing positions to an excepted-service schedule and may only initiate hiring under the authority after OPM publishes authorizations in the Federal Register (including types, numbers, and locations). For exceptions by Congress, agencies must inform OPM either before the effective date or within 30 days thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to incumbent for encumbered positions (30-day notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency that seeks to move an encumbered position from the competitive service to the excepted service (or between excepted schedules) must provide written notification to the incumbent employee of the intent to move the position 30 days prior to the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the movement is involuntary, the written notice must inform the employee that they retain any competitive status or procedural and appeal rights previously accrued under chapter 75, subchapter II, or section 4303 of title 5, and must inform the employee of appeal rights under §302.603 and the timing for exercising such rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of requirements to involuntary movement of employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of §302.602 apply to involuntary movement of competitive service or excepted service employees with respect to any earned competitive status, accrued procedural rights, or any appeal rights under chapter 75 or section 4303, even when moved to new positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This confirms that protections follow the individual employee (not only the position) when movement is involuntary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements apply even if only one position or individual is affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding plural words like “positions” or “employees,” the section applies if the directive affects only one position or one individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies cannot avoid these procedural requirements by treating a single-person action as outside the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights to MSPB for affected employees (§302.603)
rubrics_metrics.description: A competitive service employee whose position is placed into the excepted service or who is otherwise moved involuntarily to the excepted service, or an excepted service employee whose position is placed into a different schedule or who is involuntarily moved to a different schedule, may directly appeal to the Merit Systems Protection Board as provided in §302.603.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These appeals are in addition to, and not in derogation of, any right to appeal subsequent personnel actions under chapter 75 or section 4303.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds & remedies where agency asserts elimination of accrued rights (§302.603(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an agency asserts that the move will eliminate competitive status or accrued procedural and appeal rights notwithstanding §302.602, the affected individual may appeal and request an order directing the agency to correct the notice to state that accrued rights continue to apply and to comply with chapter 75 or section 4303 procedures, except to the extent inconsistent with statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief may include a correction of agency notice and an order to follow applicable statutory procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal for failure to provide requisite notice (§302.603(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency fails to comply with §302.602(c)(1) and does not provide the required 30-day written notice, the affected individual may appeal the failure and request an order directing the agency to comply with the notice requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely provision of required written notice is itself enforceable via MSPB appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealable claim of coercion for nominally voluntary moves (§302.603(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may appeal on the basis that a facially voluntary move was actually coerced or otherwise involuntary, or that a facially voluntary move would require relinquishing competitive status or protections and was coerced or involuntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves review where agencies disguise involuntary removals/transfers as voluntary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of competitive status and accrued adverse action protections when positions are listed or when employee moved involuntarily (§212.401 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee who was in the competitive service and had competitive status at the time the employee's position was first listed under Schedule A, B, or C (or other schedule created after May 9, 2024), or who was moved involuntarily to a position in the excepted service, remains in the competitive service for purposes of status and any accrued adverse action protections while occupying that position or any other position to which the employee is moved involuntarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision ensures that involuntarily moved incumbents keep their accrued protections (e.g., adverse action protections) while they remain in the position or are moved involuntarily to another position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage categories for short suspension protections (§752.201(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart B (suspension for 14 days or less) covers specific employee categories: employees who completed probation/trial period or 1 year of continuous employment (including those moved involuntarily into excepted service), employees in appointments requiring no probation who completed 1 year, Schedule B employees with competitive status (including those moved involuntarily), employees who were in competitive service and had competitive status when position first listed involuntarily under excepted schedule and still occupy that position, certain VA and GPO employees (including those moved involuntarily).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enumerates who is entitled to the short-suspension procedural protections, explicitly extending coverage to many employees involuntarily moved into excepted schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage categories for removal/suspension>14 days/reduction/furlough (§752.401(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart D covers career/career-conditional employees not serving probation, competitive-service employees meeting service thresholds (including those moved involuntarily into excepted service), certain excepted-service preference eligibles, Postal Service employees with 1 year of service in supervisory/personnel roles, nonpreference excepted-service employees with 2 years of service, Schedule B competitive-status employees, employees who had competitive status when position first listed involuntarily, and specified VA and GPO employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Again, coverage explicitly includes employees who were moved involuntarily into excepted service or to different schedules, preserving protections based on prior accrued status or service tenure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of positions determined to be confidential/policy character in coverage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple coverage provisions (e.g., §§432.102, 752.201(c)(7), 752.401(d)(2)) treat positions determined to be of a confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character differently: such positions may be excluded from certain protections unless the incumbent was moved involuntarily after accruing rights as delineated in the relevant coverage paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates an exception for political-type positions but preserves protections for incumbents who earned rights before involuntary placement in such positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability
rubrics_metrics.description: If any provision of the final rule is held invalid or unenforceable by its terms or as applied to any person or circumstance, it shall be severable from its respective section(s) and shall not affect the remainder of the rule or its application to other persons or circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If procedural requirements before moving positions are invalidated, other portions (e.g., provisions preserving protections for involuntarily moved employees) would remain independently workable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory-review determinations and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM determined: the rule is not a major economically significant rule ($200M threshold) though designated a “significant regulatory action” under EO 12866; the rule will not have substantial federalism implications (EO 13132); it meets EO 12988 standards; it will not impose unfunded mandates over $100M (Unfunded Mandates Reform Act); it will not impose paperwork/recordkeeping requirements under the Paperwork Reduction Act; and it will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities (Regulatory Flexibility Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These determinations guide agencies and reviewers about required accompanying analyses and expectations (e.g., no PRA submission required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedence and conformity to case law and statute
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule closes regulatory gaps by conforming OPM regulations to relevant Federal Circuit decisions (e.g., Van Wersch and McCormick) and statute (including conforming part 752 and clarifying subpart B), and clarifies that an employee moved to or within the excepted service retains accrued procedural and appeal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and practitioners should apply the revised regulatory language consistent with the referenced court decisions and the clarified retention of accrued rights.
